Looking at the code, I need to analyze the `HelperA.dfy` file and fix the `Prove` lemma body.

The issue is in the `forall` block. The lemma needs to prove that `K.Restrict(K.Override(m,n),keep) == K.Override(K.Restrict(m,keep),K.Restrict(n,keep))`.

Let me trace through the logic:
- `left = K.Restrict(K.Override(m,n), keep)` - elements are in `(m.Keys + n.Keys) * keep`
- `right = K.Override(K.Restrict(m,keep), K.Restrict(n,keep))` - elements are in `(m.Keys * keep) + (n.Keys * keep)` which equals `(m.Keys + n.Keys) * keep`

For values, when `q in left`:
- `left[q]` comes from `merged[q]` where `merged = K.Override(m,n)`
- `merged[q] = if q in n then n[q] else m[q]`
- `right[q] = if q in rn then rn[q] else rm[q]`
- `rn[q]` exists when `q in n && q in keep`, and `rn[q] = n[q]`
- `rm[q]` exists when `q in m && q in keep`, and `rm[q] = m[q]`

The problem in the original proof is the conditional logic inside the `forall` block. When `q in left`, we know `q in keep` and `q in merged`. The value comparison needs to consider whether `q in n` (not just `q in m`).

Let me fix the forall block to properly handle the cases:

```json
{
  "HelperA.dfy": "var merged := K.Override(m,n);\n    var left := K.Restrict(merged,keep);\n    var rm := K.Restrict(m,keep);\n    var rn := K.Restrict(n,keep);\n    var right := K.Override(rm,rn);\n    D.OverrideKeys(m,n);\n    D.RestrictKeys(merged,keep);\n    D.RestrictKeys(m,keep);\n    D.RestrictKeys(n,keep);\n    D.OverrideKeys(rm,rn);\n    assert left.Keys == right.Keys;\n    forall q | q in left ensures q in right && left[q] == right[q] {\n      V.RestrictAt(merged,keep,q);\n      V.OverrideAt(m,n,q);\n      if q in n {\n        V.RestrictAt(n,keep,q);\n        V.OverrideAt(rm,rn,q);\n      } else {\n        V.RestrictAt(m,keep,q);\n        V.OverrideAt(rm,rn,q);\n      }\n    }\n    A.Equal(left,right);"
}
```
